title: Assembly: Calling Conventions & Beyond
summary: Go from leaf functions to real programs: stack frames, recursion, libc calls, strings, SSE and SIMD, bit tricks, jump tables and a tiny virtual machine, all in hand-written x86-64.
description: You can already write small assembly functions. Now you learn how real code is organised: the System V AMD64 calling convention in full (stack arguments, callee-saved registers, stack alignment), stack frames with local variables, recursion, calling libc from assembly, arrays, structs and strings, floating point with SSE, packed SIMD arithmetic, the bit-scanning instructions, switch statements compiled into jump tables, and how to read and repair compiler output. The track ends with a stack-based bytecode interpreter written entirely in assembly. Every function is checked by hidden C programs, and where the ABI requires it they also verify that you preserved the callee-saved registers.
